weather_report:
Late morning in Osborne Park arrives bright and uncomplicated, the sun riding high with only a scatter of cloud to soften the edges. UV is punchy through midday, the sort that sneaks up on you if you linger, but the air has an easy clarity that makes colors look freshly washed. Through the afternoon those clouds will gather into a more mottled sky, light shifting from crisp to silvery and gentle by late day, still dry, still inviting.

Dress light and breathable, add sunglasses, a hat, and a streak of sunscreen if you’ll be out around lunch. It’s a good day for small, ordinary pleasures: a coffee run on foot, a quiet circuit of the neighborhood, errands by bike while the light is kind. If you’re sun-sensitive, do the outdoor bits earlier or wait for the softer midafternoon when the cloud cover takes the glare off. As evening leans in, expect a calm, tempered sky—perfect for tending a few plants on the balcony or a slow wander to clear the head before dinner.
